arxiv-2007-14329.title: On the use of GNSS for Automatic Detection of Attenuating Environments
arxiv-2007-14329.creator: Stefan Ruehrup
arxiv-2007-14329.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Stefan Ruehrup. When different radio applications share the same spectrum, the separation by attenuating material is a way to mitigate potential interference. The indoor restriction for WLAN devices in 5150-5350 MHz is an example for a regulatory measure that aims at having WLAN devices operating in an environment that provides sufficient attenuation to enable sharing with other services [ 4 ] . In this paper we investigate whether an attenuating environment can be automatically detected without user interaction.

arxiv-2509-07230.title: JOINT – Join Optimization and Inference via Network Traversal
arxiv-2509-07230.creator: Szu-Yun Ko, Bo-Cian Chang, Alan Shu-Luen Chang, Ethan Chen
arxiv-2509-07230.description: Abstract . Traditional relational databases require users to manually specify join keys and assume exact matches between column names and values. In practice, this limits joinability across fragmented or inconsistently named tables. We propose a fuzzy join framework that automatically identifies joinable column pairs and traverses indirect join paths across multiple databases.

arxiv-2512-19246.title: From Black-Box Tuning to Guided Optimization via Hyperparameters Interaction Analysis
arxiv-2512-19246.creator: 1 st Moncef Garouani, 2 nd Ayah Barhrhouj
arxiv-2512-19246.description: Abstract Hyperparameters tuning is a fundamental, yet computationally expensive, step in optimizing machine learning models. Beyond optimization, understanding the relative importance and interaction of hyperparameters is critical to efficient model development. In this paper, we introduce MetaSHAP , a scalable semi-automated eXplainable AI (XAI) method, that uses meta-learning and Shapley values analysis to provide actionable and dataset-aware tuning insights.

arxiv-2601-14130.title: GIC-DLC: Differentiable Logic Circuits for Hardware-Friendly Grayscale Image Compression
arxiv-2601-14130.creator: Till Aczel, David F. Jenny, Simon Bührer, Andreas Plesner, Antonio Di Maio, Roger Wattenhofer
arxiv-2601-14130.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Till Aczel, David F. Jenny, Simon Bührer, Andreas Plesner, Antonio Di Maio, Roger Wattenhofer. Neural image codecs achieve higher compression ratios than traditional hand-crafted methods such as PNG or JPEG-XL, but often incur substantial computational overhead, limiting their deployment on energy-constrained devices such as smartphones, cameras, and drones. We propose Grayscale Image Compression with Differentiable Logic Circuits (GIC-DLC) , a hardware-aware codec where we train lookup tables to combine the flexibility of neural networks with the efficiency of Boolean operations.

arxiv-2602-23197.title: Fine-Tuning Without Forgetting In-Context Learning: A Theoretical Analysis of Linear Attention Models
arxiv-2602-23197.creator: Chungpa Lee, Jy-yong Sohn, Kangwook Lee
arxiv-2602-23197.description: Abstract Transformer-based large language models exhibit in-context learning, enabling adaptation to downstream tasks via few-shot prompting with demonstrations. In practice, such models are often fine-tuned to improve zero-shot performance on downstream tasks, allowing them to solve tasks without examples and thereby reducing inference costs.

pmc-11644540.title: Disordered Eating Behaviors and Weight Regain in Post-Bariatric Patients
pmc-11644540.creator: Karynne Grutter Lopes, Eline Coan Romagna, Diogo Menezes Ferrazani Mattos, Luiz Guilherme Kraemer-Aguiar, Andras Hajnal
pmc-11644540.description: Background/objective: Weight regain has serious health consequences after bariatric surgery, and disordered eating behaviors (EBs) may be involved in it. We compared disordered EB symptoms in post-bariatric patients according to low vs. high ratio of weight regain (RWR) and investigated associations between disordered EB symptoms with weight regain and time since surgery.

pmc-12473235.title: A ST-ConvLSTM Network for 3D Human Keypoint Localization Using MmWave Radar
pmc-12473235.creator: Siyuan Wei, Huadong Wang, Yi Mo, Dongping Du
pmc-12473235.description: Accurate human keypoint localization in complex environments demands robust sensing and advanced modeling. In this article, we construct a ST-ConvLSTM network for 3D human keypoint estimation via millimeter-wave radar point clouds. The ST-ConvLSTM network processes multi-channel radar image inputs, generated from multi-frame fused point clouds through parallel pathways.

pmc-12886477.title: Applications of AI to single-cell and spatial transcriptomics: current state-of-the-art and challenges
pmc-12886477.creator: Boris Tchatchoua Ngassam, Huilin Niu, Sunny Pang, Valeryia Shydlouskaya, Tallulah S. Andrews
pmc-12886477.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a common tool for bioinformatics, with hundreds of methods published in recent years. Due to the training data demands of deep-learning algorithms, high-throughput single-cell and spatial transcriptomics is one of the most popular areas for these applications.

pmc-13145328.creator: L. Joensuu, V. Lukander, P. Herranen, N. P. Tynkkynen, U. Kujala, R. Lopéz‐Bueno, A. N. Nordeidet, M. Klevjer, K. Øvretveit, U. Wisløff, A. Bye, U. Ekelund, M. Ollikainen, Aarno Palotie, Aarno Palotie, Mark Daly, Bridget Riley‐Gills, Howard Jacob, Coralie Viollet, Slavé Petrovski, Alix Berton, Santh
pmc-13145328.description: We evaluated how much cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF)‐related genetics contribute to the risk of common noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) and mortality, and whether individuals with different levels of CRF and genetic predispositions differ in health characteristics. We used a validated SBayesR‐based genome‐wide polygenic score, leveraging information from 905 707 single‐nucleotide polymorphisms, to measure CRF genetics (PGS CRF).

pmc-13312586.title: Craving mediates the association between affect and substance use in daily life among individuals with substance use disorders
pmc-13312586.creator: Emmanuelle Baillet, Nicholas R. Harp, Hedy Kober, Corey Roos
pmc-13312586.description: BackgroundCraving, the desire to use substances, is a key diagnostic feature for substance use disorders (SUDs) that predicts substance use. Experiencing affective states, both positive (PA) and negative affect (NA), are also implicated in SUDs. Yet, their dynamic interrelationships with craving and substance use remain unclear, particularly at the within-person level of analysis.

pmc-13690877.title: Adjunctive use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists after bariatric surgery: updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-13690877.creator: Sakshi Arora, Fnu Amna, Fatemeh Akbarpoor, Dhvanit Rajdeep, Muhammad Khalid, Gabriel Moura Machado, Niman Maalin, Asad Ur Rehman, Marconi Abreu
pmc-13690877.description: AimsWe meta-analyzed randomized trials to assess efficacy and safety of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) after bariatric surgery.MethodsWe searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central for randomized trials comparing GLP-1 RAs with placebo after bariatric surgery. Primary outcomes were change in body weight (kg) and HbA1c (%) at 6 and 12 months.
